evidence:
The authoritative frozen workbook row 19 permits public-network fetch/install; the older internal no-network wording is superseded by the public row and skill profile. The row-specific skill requires valid LF Bash, /app installation, node entry, DB_PATH, and idempotent startup. Frozen task solution/solve.sh:1-39 has a Bash shebang, set -euo pipefail, no CR bytes, resolves its source relative to itself, checks required source files, and copies the complete app to /app. Its writes/reset targets are /app only; it contains no pkill or NODE_ENV=production. The installer checks existing default SQLite files before its closed-database reset and refuses unsafe inspection/open files (lines 9-38). Startup is node server.js, not another solve invocation, so reinstall reset is distinct from restart persistence.

Frozen environment/instructions/integration.md:5-15 requires /app/server.js, working-directory independence, 0.0.0.0:3000, health, supplied NODE_PATH, DB_PATH, and persistent records/examples. server.js:7-8 uses __dirname and DB_PATH; lines 100-102 resolve static files from that root; line 113 listens on the required address/port; lines 114-128 create the selected directory/database and use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS without inserting duplicate starter records. Seed data specifies an empty saved library, and built-in examples are ordinary packaged files. Runtime requires only Express/better-sqlite3 and Node built-ins, available in both Dockerfiles (environment:9-12, tests:16-22); compiled browser assets ship with the app.

Current installer-control/command.json binds this input hash and frozen task to image sha256:46fefc505dbcabf0d6cb4e54fea8f0880acde2f7896587750af967427598977d. probe.py:63-107 actually runs bash -n and the installer, compares all copied files, starts node /app/server.js from /tmp with sanitized declared variables, performs successful save/read controls, stops/restarts, and tests alternate DB_PATH as UID 65534. RESULTS.json records bash exit 0, exact copied-file equality, HTTP 200 health/root, successful default/alternate starts in 0.115-0.189 seconds, exact record retention after both restarts, and creation of /app/alternate/data.sqlite without default app.db. Initial/closed installs exit 0; active-root install exits 1 with the concrete open-database message. Active-unprivileged install exits 1 on EACCES, leaving both the database and saved record unchanged; this is conservative refusal, not proof it identified that process descriptor as a database. host-result.json records exit 0 in 2.75 seconds.

Current golden host RESULT.json records a completed provider-free scripted run (exit 0; 142.922 seconds, not configured judge duration). launch_workflow.py:19-23 validates frozen source hashes; lines 45-46 launch unprivileged from /tmp; lines 67-84 extract the canonical restart helper and call actual restart_app once. actual-restart.json records PID 16 to 347. post-results.json facts.S22.process_restart_durability includes equal complete pre/post collections of six saved records; S22.restart_example_inventory records all five example choices at multiplicity one before/after; S22.process_restart_write records Primary revision 2 to 3 and unchanged unrelated records. This supports actual startup/restart and idempotent example inventory without claiming an Oracle score.

Challenge cases: a reference that ignores DB_PATH could pass an adjacent-path-only smoke test. The indexed existing dbpath-probe explicitly mutates that line: its broken alternate case still saves/reads successfully but lacks the selected database, while unchanged golden server hash 17d8b0e5b9cfb56a92ddd3323dcf6d1f9d3d5dde948a809b2cbdc41694cc45a4 writes the alternate database. A conforming app may use different frontend tooling and server-relative file resolution; the public contract permits those choices, and these implementation-specific probes establish this reference behavior rather than prescribing UI selectors/routes for other submissions. No additional runtime test or process-isolation probe was run.
